title: Injecting Services
description: Learn how to inject services into controllers and other classes.

data.text: Services are typically injected through constructors. ASP.NET Core's DI container resolves dependencies automatically.

data.title: Constructor Injection

terms.definition: Passing dependencies through a class constructor.
An attribute that tells ASP.NET Core to inject a service directly into an action parameter.
A built-in service for logging, injected automatically by the DI container.

data.title: FromServices
Prefer Constructor
data.text: Prefer constructor injection for dependencies used across multiple actions. Use [FromServices] for action-specific dependencies.

data.caption: Constructor injection flow
data.definition:
graph TB
    A[DI Container] -->|Resolves| B[UsersController]
    B -->|Receives| C[IUserService]
    B -->|Receives| D[ILogger]
    C -->|Injected into| E[Actions]

data.title: Inject a Repository
data.description: Refactor a controller to use constructor injection for a repository.
steps: Replace direct instantiation with injected dependency
data.expectedOutcome: A controller that receives its repository through the constructor.

items.hint: It is the most testable and maintainable approach.
ILogger<T> is built-in and requires no registration.
Move business logic into injected services.

cards.title: [FromServices]
cards.description: Dependency injected directly into an action parameter.

data.title: Key Takeaways
data.takeaway: Constructor injection is the preferred approach.
